reason: E2 shows that low-temperature annealing precipitates L1₂ in the FCC phase of a similar lamellar eutectic HEA and that Orowan strengthening occurs, supporting the first two premises. However, neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence that precipitates form preferentially near interfaces, that they interrupt dislocation pile-ups, or that this mechanism enhances ductility; E1 uses cryo-rolling to create a hierarchical grain structure, not precipitation, and E2 explicitly states ductility was not affected. Thus, the core mechanistic premises about pile-up mitigation and ductility gain are unsupported.
premises: Low-temperature annealing of a lamellar FCC+B2 eutectic HEA can precipitate coherent L1₂ within the FCC phase
These L1₂ precipitates strengthen the alloy via an Orowan bypass mechanism
The precipitation can be induced specifically near phase boundaries to interrupt dislocation pile-ups
Interrupting pile-ups reduces local stress concentrations and microcracking, enhancing ductility
A single-step anneal after moderate deformation yields simultaneous strength and ductility improvement
